# lowob

> Commercial growth for complex markets: strategy, growth, distribution and revenue.

## Core pages

- [Operator experience. Studio flexibility.](https://lowob.com/about/): Senior commercial judgment and studio flexibility for complex markets.
- [Tell us where the business is getting stuck.](https://lowob.com/contact/): Tell lowob where the business is getting stuck and send a focused commercial brief.
- [Distribution](https://lowob.com/distribution/): Distribution services from lowob: Put real distribution behind the strategy.
- [Growth](https://lowob.com/growth/): Growth services from lowob: Turn the strategy into activity people can see, understand, and act on.
- [Commercial growth for complex markets](https://lowob.com/): lowob connects strategy, growth, distribution, partnerships and revenue to help companies build commercial traction in AI, Web3, fintech, media and technology.
- [Privacy policy](https://lowob.com/privacy/): What we collect when you send a brief or read the site; why; who sees it; and how to ask us to stop.
- [Useful research. Clearer decisions.](https://lowob.com/research/): Practical Lowob research across strategy, growth, distribution, and revenue in complex markets.
- [Revenue](https://lowob.com/revenue/): Revenue services from lowob: Convert market activity into commercial traction.
- [Strategy](https://lowob.com/strategy/): Strategy services from lowob: Understand the market before trying to scale into it.
- [Four Functions, One Commercial Solution](https://lowob.com/system/): Explore the lowob commercial system: integrated strategy, growth, distribution, partnerships and revenue execution for complex markets.
- [Terms of use](https://lowob.com/terms/): The terms for reading lowob.com and its Research. Client engagements run on a written scope, which takes precedence over anything here.

## Research

- ["40,000 members and nobody does anything"](https://lowob.com/research/40-000-members-and-nobody-does-anything/): A large, silent community was recruited for a payout and never given a job.
- [A loop with good context](https://lowob.com/research/a-loop-with-good-context/): An agent is a loop, and the context it most needs is prior judgment on comparable cases. How to add a precedent slot, and how to test it blind.
- [A reviewer who does not verify is not a control](https://lowob.com/research/a-reviewer-who-does-not-verify-is-not-a-control/): Human-in-the-loop is a design pattern, not a defence. Courts, regulators and clients now look for evidence that the human actually checked.
- [Account Planning for the Top Twenty](https://lowob.com/research/account-planning-for-the-top-twenty/): How a mid-size firm picks its top twenty accounts by growth potential, keeps one-page plans current, and reviews them monthly so they shape real decisions.
- [Ad Network vs Ad Exchange vs DSP: The Middlemen](https://lowob.com/research/ad-network-vs-exchange-vs-dsp/): Ad networks, ad exchanges, and DSPs all sit between your budget and a publisher. What each does, how each is paid, and which one you are actually dealing with.
- [Build an Affiliate Program Without Paying for Coupon Leaks](https://lowob.com/research/affiliate-program-asset-or-coupon-leak/): Playbook from lowob Research: Your Affiliate Program Is Either an Asset You Own or a Coupon Leak You Pay For.
- [Affiliate vs Partner vs Referral Programs: What's the Difference?](https://lowob.com/research/affiliate-vs-partner-vs-referral/): Affiliate, partner and referral programs all pay third parties to bring customers. How each works, who runs it, and which one a company needs.
- [Agency Types Explained: Full-Service to Specialist](https://lowob.com/research/agency-types-field-guide/): Not all agencies do the same work. A field guide to the main types, what each is good at, how each is paid, and the questions that reveal which one you need.
- [Agency vs Consultancy vs Advisor vs Fractional: Explained](https://lowob.com/research/agency-vs-consultancy-vs-advisor/): What an agency, a consultancy, an advisor and a fractional executive each sell, how each is paid, and which problem each one fits.
- [Agentic AI vs Generative AI: What Changes When the Model Can Act](https://lowob.com/research/agentic-ai-vs-generative-ai/): Generative AI produces content for a person to use. Agentic AI pursues a goal and acts in your systems. What changes is risk, controls, cost and the record.
- [AI Agent vs Chatbot: The Difference That Matters to a Buyer](https://lowob.com/research/ai-agent-vs-chatbot/): A chatbot answers in a conversation. An AI agent works toward a goal and acts in your systems. For a buyer, the difference is liability, controls and price.
- [AI Agents in Commercial Operations: The RevOps Tasks Worth Handing Over](https://lowob.com/research/ai-agents-in-commercial-operations/): Twelve RevOps tasks rated for how far an AI agent can take them today, the risk, the control, where each sits in the brain, and the first three to hand over.
- [AI Agents in Customer Success and Account Management](https://lowob.com/research/ai-agents-in-customer-success-and-account-management/): Nine customer success and account tasks rated for how far an AI agent can take them today, the main risk, the control, and where each plugs into the brain.
- [AI Agents in Marketing: What They Can Do Now, Task by Task](https://lowob.com/research/ai-agents-in-marketing-what-they-can-do-now/): Thirteen marketing tasks rated for how far an AI agent can take them today, the main risk, the control, where each fits in the brain and where to start.
- [AI Agents in Partners and Distribution: What Works and What Leaks](https://lowob.com/research/ai-agents-in-partners-and-distribution/): Nine partner and channel tasks rated for how far an AI agent can take them today, the main risk, the control, and where each plugs into the brain.
- [AI Agents in Sales: What They Can Do Now, Task by Task](https://lowob.com/research/ai-agents-in-sales-what-they-can-do-now/): Seventeen sales tasks rated for how far an AI agent can take them today, the main risk, the control, where each plugs into the brain and where to start.
- [AI Companies Have a Distribution Problem Disguised as a Model Problem.](https://lowob.com/research/ai-companies-distribution-problem/): Analysis from lowob Research: AI Companies Have a Distribution Problem Disguised as a Model Problem.
- [AI Copilot vs AI Agent: What Is the Difference?](https://lowob.com/research/ai-copilot-vs-ai-agent/): An AI copilot assists a person who stays in control of each step. An AI agent works toward a goal, choosing its steps and acting through tools within limits.
- [AI Did Not Fix Your Marketing. It Made Your Mediocrity Cheaper.](https://lowob.com/research/ai-made-average-marketing-cheaper/): Analysis from lowob Research: AI Did Not Fix Your Marketing. It Made Your Mediocrity Cheaper.
- [Airdrops Can Buy Attention. They Cannot Buy Belief.](https://lowob.com/research/airdrops-points-community-incentives/): Analysis from lowob Research: Airdrops Can Buy Attention. They Cannot Buy Belief.
- [An audience is not a business](https://lowob.com/research/an-audience-is-not-a-business/): An audience is an asset, not a business. A media business starts when you can say who the audience is, who pays for access to it, and which part you own.
- [Approval rate measures fatigue too](https://lowob.com/research/approval-rate-measures-fatigue-too/): "Accepted without edit" rises when an AI system improves. It also rises when reviewers get tired, trust fluency, stop seeing hard cases, or ask for less.
- [Ask for the gap, not the summary](https://lowob.com/research/ask-for-the-gap-not-the-summary/): A good judgment system doesn't ask people to tell it everything. It knows what the next decision needs, spots what's missing, and asks one specific question.
- [Attribution vs Incrementality: What Did Your Marketing Actually Cause?](https://lowob.com/research/attribution-vs-incrementality/): Analysis from lowob Research: Attribution Is a Story You Tell Your CFO. Incrementality Is What Happened.
- [Below the volume floor](https://lowob.com/research/below-the-volume-floor/): At 150 decisions a year, all different, no model will learn your judgment, and pooling across companies does not rescue it.
- [Brand Safety vs Brand Suitability: What They Cost You](https://lowob.com/research/brand-safety-and-suitability/): Brand safety avoids harm; brand suitability judges fit. How verification enforces both, what over-blocking costs, and how to set standards that protect reach.
- [Brand vs Performance Marketing: Different Time Horizons](https://lowob.com/research/brand-vs-performance-marketing/): Brand versus performance is mostly a misunderstanding. What each does, over what time, how they interact, and how a small company should split its budget.
- [Build it to run without you](https://lowob.com/research/build-it-to-run-without-you/): A GTM system is only an asset if the company owns it: the accounts, the records, the routines and the reasons.
- [Build vs Buy AI Agents: A Decision Guide for Mid-Size Firms](https://lowob.com/research/build-vs-buy-ai-agents/): Most firms now buy AI rather than build it. For a mid-size firm, buy the agent and the wiring, and own the record of decisions and outcomes it produces.
- [Building the Commercial System at 20, 50 and 200 People](https://lowob.com/research/building-the-commercial-system-at-every-size/): The capstone of The Commercial System: what strategy, growth, distribution and revenue should look like at 20, 50 and 200 people, and what to leave until later.
- [Built to be kept without us](https://lowob.com/research/built-to-be-kept-without-us/): The honest test of any judgment system, and of anyone who installs one, is whether it keeps working after they leave.
- [Buy Context. Own Judgment. What Enterprise AI Teams Should Build](https://lowob.com/research/buy-context-own-judgment-what-to-build-at-each-size/): At every size, the same rule holds: rent the context layer as it matures, and own the record of how you decide.
- [Calibration is the honest learning signal](https://lowob.com/research/calibration-is-the-honest-learning-signal/): A system cannot claim to learn by grading its own outputs. It can by comparing human predictions with outcomes it did not produce.
- [Campaign Testing That Reaches a Decision](https://lowob.com/research/campaign-testing-that-reaches-a-decision/): Most B2B campaign tests are too small to decide anything. Sample sizes at B2B volumes, choosing the metric, holdouts, and writing the decision before the test.
- [Channel Conflict, and How to Manage It](https://lowob.com/research/channel-conflict-and-how-to-manage-it/): Channel conflict is a rules problem before it is a people problem. Where it comes from, what the evidence says it costs, and the rules that keep it small.

- [Co-Selling With Platforms](https://lowob.com/research/co-selling-with-platforms/): Co-selling with a cloud platform works when your product grows the platform&#x27;s own number. How the programmes work, what they cost, and how to earn referrals.
- [Commercial KPIs a Board Will Trust](https://lowob.com/research/commercial-kpis-a-board-will-trust/): A board trusts a commercial KPI when it is defined once, reconciled to finance, stable over time and owned. Eight measures that pass, and how to report them.
- [Community is a job, not a number](https://lowob.com/research/community-is-a-job-not-a-number/): A community earns its keep by doing work the company would otherwise pay for.
- [Community that survives the airdrop](https://lowob.com/research/community-that-survives-the-airdrop/): Incentives buy activity, not community. Build for the people who stay when the payments stop, give them a job, and keep their record on channels you own.
- [Audience vs Community: What Actually Makes the Difference?](https://lowob.com/research/community-vs-audience/): Analysis from lowob Research: Your "Community" Is Probably Just an Audience With a Chat Room.
- [Community Management vs Social Media Management](https://lowob.com/research/community-vs-social-media-management/): Community management and social media management are different disciplines. What each does, what each measures, and how to staff them without failure.
- [Content With a Job](https://lowob.com/research/content-with-a-job/): Give every B2B content piece a job: a named reader, the decision it serves, a stage, a next action and a retirement date. How to brief, measure and prune.
- [CPM, CPC, CPA, CPL, ROAS Explained: Which to Run On](https://lowob.com/research/cpm-cpc-cpa-cpl-roas-explained/): CPM, CPC, CPA, CPL and ROAS explained: what each measures, what each hides, and the one number a company should actually manage to.

- [Demand Generation Economics](https://lowob.com/research/demand-generation-economics/): How to run B2B demand generation on unit economics: cost per qualified opportunity, CAC payback, the capture and creation split, and a budget ceiling.

- [How Marketing Tracking Works: Pixels to Server-Side](https://lowob.com/research/how-marketing-tracking-works/): Pixels, cookies, first-party data, server-side tracking and consent, explained plainly, and what a company should own whoever runs its media.
- [How to Measure AI ROI in a Commercial Team](https://lowob.com/research/how-to-measure-ai-roi/): Measure AI ROI in sales and marketing by valuing the decisions AI informs, writing back outcomes against a comparison, and netting off tool and review time.
- [How to Read a Creator Media Kit](https://lowob.com/research/how-to-read-a-creator-media-kit/): A media kit is a sales document. What each number means, which figures are routinely inflated, and the questions to ask before agreeing to a creator's rate.
- [How to Read a Media Plan Before You Approve It](https://lowob.com/research/how-to-read-a-media-plan/): A media plan says where a budget goes, when and why. What a good one contains, what the columns mean, and what to ask before signing off.
- [How to Run a Marketing RFP Without Wasting a Quarter](https://lowob.com/research/how-to-run-a-marketing-rfp/): Most marketing RFPs select for the best proposal writer. What an RFP should contain, how to evaluate responses, and a shorter process that finds the partner.
- [How to Write an Ideal Customer Profile Sales Will Use](https://lowob.com/research/how-to-write-an-icp/): An ideal customer profile describes who is most likely to buy, succeed, and stay. What an ICP contains, how it differs from a persona, and how to build one.
- [Human-in-the-Loop vs Human-on-the-Loop](https://lowob.com/research/human-in-the-loop-vs-human-on-the-loop/): In the loop, a person approves before an AI action takes effect. On the loop, the system acts and a person monitors and can stop it. Which fits each task.
- [Influencer vs Creator vs KOL vs Ambassador: Definitions](https://lowob.com/research/influencer-creator-kol-ambassador/): Influencers, creators, KOLs and ambassadors are not the same thing. What each one is, how each is paid, and how the deal structure should differ.
- [Integrators, OEMs and channel partners](https://lowob.com/research/integrators-oems-and-channel-partners/): In emerging tech the buyer already trusts someone else's hands; your job is to make those hands want to carry you, one partner at a time.
- [Intent Data vs First-Party Data](https://lowob.com/research/intent-data-vs-first-party-data/): Intent data infers which companies are researching a topic; first-party data is what buyers do with you directly. How the two differ, and which to use first.
- [Intent, not a destination](https://lowob.com/research/intent-not-a-destination/): Every interaction a judgment system records should serve an explicit outcome. But naming the conclusion in advance bends the reasoning to reach it.
- [Issuers, integrations and curators](https://lowob.com/research/issuers-integrations-and-curators/): When paid channels are closed, crypto distribution comes from people who already want you to succeed: issuers, integrations, curators and ecosystems.
- [AI Is Making Execution Cheap. Judgment Is Becoming the Marketing Moat.](https://lowob.com/research/judgment-is-the-moat/): AI / Marketing from lowob Research: AI Is Making Execution Cheap. Judgment Is Becoming the Marketing Moat.
- [Keep the sources; let the summary regenerate](https://lowob.com/research/keep-the-sources-let-the-summary-regenerate/): A generated summary must never be the only surviving copy of a decision. Every summary is a lossy compression made by one model on one day.
- [Landing Pages and Ad Review: Why Yours Gets Rejected](https://lowob.com/research/landing-pages-and-ad-review/): A landing page is reviewed by the ad platform before the visitor sees it. What it should contain, why restricted pages get rejected, how to pass and convert.
- [Lead Scoring vs Account Scoring](https://lowob.com/research/lead-scoring-vs-account-scoring/): Lead scoring ranks individual people; account scoring ranks companies by fit and buying-group engagement. How they differ, and how to combine the two.
- [LLM Observability vs Application Monitoring](https://lowob.com/research/llm-observability-vs-apm/): Application monitoring tells you whether a service is up and fast. LLM observability tells you whether its answers and actions were right, and what they cost.
- [LLM Optimization Checklist for Content and Marketing](https://lowob.com/research/llm-optimization-checklist/): Practical steps to make a company more likely to be cited by AI assistants: page structure, claims, corroboration, third-party presence and measurement.
- [Long Context Windows vs RAG](https://lowob.com/research/long-context-vs-rag/): Long context puts whole documents into the prompt; RAG retrieves only the relevant parts. Research finds trade-offs in accuracy, cost and control.
- [LTV:CAC vs CAC Payback: Which Unit Economics Metric to Trust](https://lowob.com/research/ltv-cac-vs-cac-payback/): LTV:CAC compares lifetime profit with the cost to win a customer; CAC payback counts months to recover that cost. Formulas, an example and which to trust.
- [Market Maps That Sales Actually Uses](https://lowob.com/research/market-maps-that-sales-actually-uses/): A market map sales uses is a list of named accounts in the CRM, tiered, with triggers, owners and status. How to build one and keep it current.
- [Marketplace Listings for B2B Sellers](https://lowob.com/research/marketplace-listings-for-b2b/): A cloud marketplace listing is a procurement route more than a discovery channel. When it pays, how private offers work, and the costs B2B sellers miss.
- [MCP vs A2A: How the Two Agent Protocols Fit Together](https://lowob.com/research/mcp-vs-a2a/): MCP connects an AI agent to tools and data. A2A lets one agent hand a task to another. How the two protocols fit together, and what to ask vendors about each.
- [MCP vs API Integrations: What Changes and What Does Not](https://lowob.com/research/mcp-vs-api-integrations/): An API integration is code a developer writes against one system. MCP lets an AI model discover and call tools at run time. What changes, and what does not.
- [Measuring Brand in B2B](https://lowob.com/research/measuring-brand-in-b2b/): Most B2B buyers rank vendors before they speak to one. How to measure brand where attribution cannot see: share of search, shortlist rate and entry points.
- [Membership is the job](https://lowob.com/research/membership-is-the-job/): A media audience is a list until it is a membership; build the membership on sourcing, amplification and peer value, then measure it like a business line.
- [Native Advertising and Sponsored Content Explained](https://lowob.com/research/native-advertising-and-sponsored-content/): Native advertising and sponsored content are paid placements that fit their surroundings. What each is, what disclosure requires, and when they beat plain ads.
- [NIST AI RMF vs ISO/IEC 42001](https://lowob.com/research/nist-ai-rmf-vs-iso-42001/): The NIST AI RMF is free, voluntary guidance on AI risk. ISO/IEC 42001 is a certifiable management system standard. Most firms use NIST to plan and ISO to prove.
- [Gateway 1: Nothing Sends Without a Person](https://lowob.com/research/nothing-sends-without-a-person/): How to design human-in-the-loop approval for AI agents: who approves what, what to log, and how to stop review becoming a rubber stamp.
- [NRR vs GRR: Which Retention Number to Report](https://lowob.com/research/nrr-vs-grr/): NRR counts expansion and can exceed 100%; GRR counts only what was kept and cannot. Formulas, a worked example, benchmarks, and why to report both together.

- [What Is a Decision Record?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-decision-record/): A decision record is a short, dated entry for one decision: what was decided, why, who owns it, its status and the outcome expected. How to write one well.

- [What Is a Golden Record?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-golden-record/): A golden record is the single trusted version of a customer, account or product, built from matched source records by rules that pick each field&#x27;s value.
- [What Is a Knowledge Graph (for AI)?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-knowledge-graph/): A knowledge graph stores facts as entities and their relationships, so AI can follow connections that text search misses. How it works and when it helps.
- [What Is a Large Language Model (LLM)?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-large-language-model/): A large language model is AI trained on vast text to predict the next token, so it can write, summarise and answer. How it works, what it costs, where it fails.

- [What Is CAC Payback?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-cac-payback/): CAC payback is the number of months a new customer takes to repay what it cost to win them, measured on gross profit. It shows how long growth ties up cash.

- [What Is Excessive Agency in AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-excessive-agency/): Excessive agency means an AI system has more tools, permissions or autonomy than its task needs, so one error or manipulation does real damage. How to scope it.

- [What Is Pipeline Coverage?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-pipeline-coverage/): Pipeline coverage is open pipeline value divided by the revenue target for a period. The right ratio depends on your own win rate, not a 3x rule of thumb.
- [What Is Product-Led Growth?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-product-led-growth/): Product-led growth is a go-to-market motion in which the product acquires, converts and expands customers, with sales joining later. When it fits.

- [What Is Prompt Caching?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-prompt-caching/): Prompt caching reuses the processed start of a prompt across AI requests, so repeated input costs less and runs faster. How it works, and how to design for it.

- [What Is Retargeting, and Why It Overclaims Credit](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-retargeting/): Retargeting shows ads to people who already visited. How it works, why its reported results are almost always inflated, and how to run it without paying twice.
- [What Is Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-retrieval-augmented-generation/): RAG lets an AI model look up relevant documents before answering, so responses draw on your data. How it works, where it fails and how to evaluate a RAG system.
- [What Is Revenue Intelligence?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-revenue-intelligence/): Revenue intelligence software joins CRM data to captured emails, meetings and calls to score deals, inspect pipeline and support forecasts. How to judge it.

- [What Is Reverse ETL?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-reverse-etl/): Reverse ETL copies modelled data from a data warehouse into the CRM and other tools teams work in. How it works, what it is for, and how to sync it safely.
- [What Is Robotic Process Automation (RPA) in the Age of Agents?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-robotic-process-automation/): RPA is software that copies a person&#x27;s clicks and keystrokes to run rule-based tasks across apps, often where no API exists. How it fits beside AI agents.
- [What Is Sales Forecasting, and Why Is It Usually Wrong?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-sales-forecasting/): Sales forecasting estimates the revenue a team will close in a period. Why most forecasts miss, the main forecasting methods, and how to make one more honest.
- [What Is Sales Velocity?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-sales-velocity/): Sales velocity is how much revenue a sales pipeline produces per day: opportunities times deal size times win rate, divided by the sales cycle length in days.
- [What Is Seat-Based Pricing for AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-seat-based-pricing-for-ai/): Seat-based pricing charges a fixed fee per named user per month for an AI tool. What a seat includes, why agents strain the model, and how to buy seats well.

- [What Is Shadow AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-shadow-ai/): Shadow AI is staff using AI tools the company has not approved or cannot see. Why it happens, what it costs in breaches, and how to bring it into the open.
- [What Is Structured Output in AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-structured-output/): Structured output makes an AI model answer in a fixed schema, usually JSON, so software can read it. What it guarantees, what it does not, and how to use it.
- [What Is Synthetic Data?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-synthetic-data/): Synthetic data is artificial data generated to mirror the patterns of real data. Where it helps, where it can still expose people, and where it misleads.
- [What Are TAM, SAM and SOM?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-tam-sam-som/): TAM, SAM and SOM are nested market-size estimates: total demand, the part you can serve, and the share you can win. Built bottom-up, they set real targets.
- [What Is the Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-the-agent2agent-protocol/): A2A is an open protocol that lets AI agents from different vendors find each other, hand off tasks and report status. How it works and how it differs from MCP.
- [What Is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-the-model-context-protocol/): MCP is an open standard for connecting AI assistants and agents to tools and data. How it works, who supports it, its security risks and how to use it.
- [What Is the NIST AI Risk Management Framework?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-the-nist-ai-risk-management-framework/): The NIST AI RMF is voluntary US guidance for managing AI risk through four functions: govern, map, measure and manage. What it asks and how to use it.
- [What Is UGC, and Why Brands Now Pay for It](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-ugc/): UGC now means genuine customer content and paid creator content styled to look organic. What each is, how it is used in ads, and the disclosure rules.
- [What Is Usage-Based Pricing for AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-usage-based-pricing-for-ai/): Usage-based pricing for AI charges for the volume of work done, such as actions, tokens or credits, rather than per user. How it works and how to buy it well.
- [What Is Value-Based Pricing?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-value-based-pricing/): Value-based pricing sets price from the value an offer creates for a buyer against their next best option, not from cost or rivals&#x27; prices. How it works.
- [What Is Win-Loss Analysis?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-win-loss-analysis/): Win-loss analysis is the structured study of why deals are won or lost, using buyer interviews and deal data, so findings shape positioning and process.
- [What Is Zero Data Retention in AI?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-zero-data-retention/): Zero data retention means an AI provider does not store your prompts and outputs after responding. What it covers, which features it excludes and what to ask.
- [What Makes a Case Study Believable](https://lowob.com/research/what-makes-a-case-study-believable/): Case studies are evidence, not advertising. What a believable one contains, why most are not believed, and the version that works without naming the client.
- [What SEO Is Now: How Search Ranking Works Today](https://lowob.com/research/what-seo-is-now/): SEO has changed more in three years than in the previous ten. How ranking works today, what still matters, what stopped, and how AI answers change the job.
- [What Thought Leadership Actually Is](https://lowob.com/research/what-thought-leadership-actually-is/): Thought leadership is a defensible position with evidence and consequence. Why most of it is neither, how it differs from content marketing, how to make it.
- [What We Would Cut From the Build Order](https://lowob.com/research/what-we-would-cut-from-the-build-order/): An honest review of The Build Order: which steps are overbuilt for firms under 50 people, what to skip, and what the evidence says about over-engineering AI.
- [Where judgment arrives first](https://lowob.com/research/where-judgment-arrives-first/): Judgment layers will work first where decisions are frequent, similar and graded quickly, and where someone will later have to defend them.
- [Which AI Assistant, Which Seats](https://lowob.com/research/which-ai-assistant-which-seats/): How to choose between Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini for business: suite fit, connectors, controls and logging matter more than benchmarks.
- [Whoever holds the record holds the company](https://lowob.com/research/whoever-holds-the-record-holds-the-company/): The layer that encodes how a business decides is the deepest lock-in in enterprise software. It is also where the strongest growth is.
- [Why the Brain Starts at the Commercial Line](https://lowob.com/research/why-the-brain-starts-at-the-commercial-line/): Start an enterprise AI build where you can count what changed within a quarter. Why that is sales and marketing, the evidence, and when the order bends.
- [Running a Win-Loss Programme](https://lowob.com/research/win-loss-programmes/): How a 20 to 500 person firm runs win-loss as a standing programme: which deals to sample, who interviews, how to code answers and where each finding is decided.
- [Workflow Automation vs AI Agents: Which Do You Need?](https://lowob.com/research/workflow-automation-vs-ai-agents/): Workflow automation runs fixed steps a person designed. An AI agent chooses its own steps toward a goal. How to tell which a commercial process needs.
- [You don't have three problems](https://lowob.com/research/you-dont-have-three-problems/): Fundraising, community and customer acquisition are three outputs of one commercial system.
- [Your CRM Is Memory, Not a Brain](https://lowob.com/research/your-crm-is-memory-not-a-brain/): A CRM stores what happened; it does not think. The fields AI needs, a one-week clean-up, and how to pick a CRM people keep current.
- [Your first ten customers are design partners](https://lowob.com/research/your-first-ten-customers-are-design-partners/): Pick early customers for fit and learning, not logos. Agree a written success test, work closely for six to twelve weeks, then convert the ones that succeed.
- [Your first ten sponsors are design partners](https://lowob.com/research/your-first-ten-sponsors-are-design-partners/): Sponsorship, data and research are B2B sales. Treat the first ten buyers as design partners: agree the test and the report before money moves.
